title: The work queue under concurrency: claiming, fencing, expiry, LISTEN/NOTIFY
question: Does the D6 §3 claim statement with attempt fencing hold under concurrent worker processes, an abrupt kill and a stalled worker, and does LISTEN/NOTIFY with a timeout wake workers without lost wake-ups?
method: 10,000 pending tasks; worker processes with their own connections claiming batches of 50 with the D6 §3 / store note §4 statement (lease 2 s), completing in one transaction (fencing UPDATE on id and attempt, binary COPY of observations with Copy.set_types, outcome); W1 SIGKILLed holding its third batch; Z stalls 2.5 leases without renewing then tries to complete; W2 throughout, waiting on LISTEN cs_task_ready with a 1 s timeout; then 100 tasks with NOTIFY in the inserting transaction and 100 without. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Ubuntu 18.6-1.pgdg24.04+2), pg_textsearch 1.5.1, vector 0.8.7, on the project-local cluster (just db-up; socket build/pg/run, port 5440, pg_textsearch preloaded); DDL applied and rows written as the NOLOGIN non-superuser cs_s6_app (SET ROLE) in cs_spike_s6 cloned from cs_template; psycopg 3.3.6 (binary), pgvector-python 0.5.1, spike venv checked against the lock (`uv sync --locked --check`: no changes) before the final run; free disk 109G at start, 106G at end.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6_*, code/s6*.py/.sql, results/s6/, records/s6.*

results.name: reclaimed_tasks
results.note: exactly W1's in-flight batch (50) and Z's batch (50), by the ordinary claim (no reaper), attempt 2

results.name: stalled_worker_fenced_in
results.note: its late write committed no observation

results.name: notify_commit_to_claim
results.note: below the client timer's resolution here; the notified batch done in 0.045 s

results.name: silent_insert_to_claim
results.note: found by the timeout re-query (timeout 1 s)

results.name: claim_plan
results.value: BitmapOr of task_pending and task_lease, then a sort of every qualifying row before LIMIT
results.note: the OR keeps the claim off task_pending's (priority DESC, id) order

conclusion: The claim statement with attempt fencing holds: 10,200 tasks done exactly once, no claim while a lease was live, the killed worker's and the stalled worker's batches re-claimed only after expiry by the ordinary claim, and the stalled worker's late write fenced out with nothing committed. LISTEN before the re-check plus a timed wait wakes at once on NOTIFY and finds un-notified work at the timeout. The claim's OR across pending and expired rows plans as a BitmapOr plus a full sort of qualifying rows, cheap at 10⁴ pending tasks per stage but a candidate for two branches at larger queues.
